evidence: src/presentation/controllers/AppointmentsController.ts: book() contains `if (form.minutes < 10 || form.minutes > 120) { throw new SchedulingError('rejected', 'A visit lasts between 10 and 120 minutes'); }`. This is a domain rule about allowed visit length.
The rule is enforced before calling `this.scheduling.book(...)`, so `SchedulingService` (business/domain) is not the only place that guards appointment duration.
cancel() and addNote() only call services and format results, which fits the presentation role.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The presentation-layer controller is supposed to take in form data, call the business services and pass the results to the presenter. Most of it does that: `cancel` and `addNote` just call services and format the result. `book` is the problem. It checks that a visit lasts between 10 and 120 minutes and throws the domain's own `SchedulingError('rejected', ...)` if it doesn't. That limit is a scheduling rule, not a check on the form's format, so it belongs in `SchedulingService` or an Appointment entity. As written, the controller holds part of the domain logic, and any other caller of `SchedulingService.book` would skip the check.

violations.message: AppointmentsController.book() enforces the business rule that a visit lasts 10 to 120 minutes and throws the domain SchedulingError('rejected'). This rule belongs in the business (domain) layer, such as SchedulingService.book or an Appointment entity, not in a presentation controller.
